relationshipTypes.label: prerequisite for
relationshipTypes.description: Understanding the source concept helps with the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: supports
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept provides a result or tool used by the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: special case of
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept is a more specific form of the target concept.

relationshipTypes.label: counterpart of
relationshipTypes.description: The concepts play related roles in different inferential approaches.

relationshipTypes.label: method for
relationshipTypes.description: The source concept is a method used to carry out the target task.

nodes.label: Probability theory
nodes.description: The mathematical language used to describe uncertainty.

nodes.label: Events and set operations
nodes.description: Events, complements, intersections and unions within a sample space.

nodes.label: Conditional probability
nodes.description: Probability updated after learning that another event occurred.

nodes.label: Independence
nodes.description: A relationship in which learning about one event does not change the probability of another.

nodes.label: Law of total probability
nodes.description: Decomposes a probability across an exhaustive partition.

nodes.label: Bayes’ theorem
nodes.description: Reverses a conditional probability using a prior probability and the law of total probability.

nodes.label: Random variables
nodes.description: Numerical quantities whose values are governed by probability.

nodes.label: Expectation
nodes.description: The probability-weighted population mean of a random variable.

nodes.label: Variance
nodes.description: The expected squared deviation of a random variable from its mean.

nodes.label: Covariance and correlation
nodes.description: Measures of how two random variables vary together.

nodes.label: Addition rule and inclusion–exclusion
nodes.description: Find the probability of a union without counting the overlap twice.

nodes.label: Mutually exclusive events and partitions
nodes.description: Disjoint, exhaustive events divide a sample space into non-overlapping possibilities.

nodes.label: Cumulative distribution functions
nodes.description: A CDF gives the probability of a value at or below each threshold.

nodes.label: Probability mass functions
nodes.description: A PMF assigns probabilities to individual values of a discrete random variable.

nodes.label: Probability density functions
nodes.description: A PDF gives continuous probabilities through areas, rather than density heights.

nodes.label: Joint distributions
nodes.description: A joint PMF or PDF describes several random variables and their dependence.

nodes.label: Marginal distributions
nodes.description: Sum or integrate a joint distribution over the variables not being considered.

nodes.label: Conditional distributions
nodes.description: Restrict and normalise a joint distribution after observing another variable.

nodes.label: Moments and expectations of functions
nodes.description: Compute population summaries such as E[X²] using sums or integrals.

nodes.label: Convergence in probability
nodes.description: The probability of a fixed-size deviation from the limit tends to zero.

nodes.label: Convergence in distribution
nodes.description: Distribution functions approach a limiting distribution at its continuity points.

nodes.label: Chebyshev’s inequality
nodes.description: Bounds a tail probability using variance; useful in consistency proofs.

nodes.label: Statistical inference
nodes.description: Learning about an unknown population or mechanism using observed data.

nodes.label: Population, sample and data
nodes.description: The distinction between the target population, sampled units and recorded observations.

nodes.label: Statistical models
nodes.description: Probability distributions indexed by parameters and used to represent data-generating processes.

nodes.label: Random samples and i.i.d. assumptions
nodes.description: A random sample consists of independent observations with a common distribution.

nodes.label: Types of data
nodes.description: Distinguish numerical, categorical, discrete, continuous and multivariate data.

nodes.label: Philosophies of inference
nodes.description: The different interpretations and procedures used to learn from data.

nodes.label: Frequentist inference
nodes.description: Treats parameters as fixed and evaluates procedures through repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Bayesian inference
nodes.description: Represents uncertainty about parameters using probability distributions.

nodes.label: Inference tasks
nodes.description: Point estimation, interval estimation and hypothesis testing.

nodes.label: Estimators and estimates
nodes.description: Statistics used to estimate unknown population parameters.

nodes.label: Sampling distributions
nodes.description: The probability distribution of a statistic under repeated sampling.

nodes.label: Bias
nodes.description: The systematic difference between an estimator’s expectation and its target.

nodes.label: Standard error
nodes.description: The standard deviation of an estimator’s sampling distribution.

nodes.label: Mean squared error
nodes.description: A loss criterion combining an estimator’s variance and squared bias.

nodes.label: Central limit theorem
nodes.description: Explains why suitably scaled sample means are approximately Normal in large samples.

nodes.label: Consistency
nodes.description: An estimator approaches the true parameter as the sample size grows.

nodes.label: Sample mean
nodes.description: Average the observations to estimate a population mean.

nodes.label: Sample variance
nodes.description: The usual sample variance uses n − 1 to give an unbiased estimate of population variance.

nodes.label: Variance of an estimator
nodes.description: Measures the spread of an estimator across repeated samples.

nodes.label: Bias–variance decomposition
nodes.description: Mean squared error equals estimator variance plus squared bias.

nodes.label: Asymptotic unbiasedness
nodes.description: An estimator’s bias tends to zero as sample size grows.

nodes.label: Likelihood
nodes.description: The statistical model viewed as a function of its unknown parameter for fixed observed data.

nodes.label: Sufficiency
nodes.description: Data reduction that retains all model information about a parameter.

nodes.label: Maximum likelihood estimation
nodes.description: Chooses the parameter value that maximises the likelihood.

nodes.label: Log-likelihood
nodes.description: A logarithmic transformation of likelihood that simplifies products and optimisation.

nodes.label: Score statistic
nodes.description: The derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to the parameter.

nodes.label: Fisher information
nodes.description: Quantifies how much information the model carries about a parameter.

nodes.label: Cramér–Rao lower bound
nodes.description: A lower bound on the variance of unbiased estimators under regularity conditions.

nodes.label: Asymptotic distribution of the MLE
nodes.description: The large-sample Normal approximation for maximum likelihood estimators.

nodes.label: Likelihood with dependent observations
nodes.description: Use the joint model or conditional factorisation; a product of marginal densities requires independence.

nodes.label: MLE with several parameters
nodes.description: Maximise a likelihood jointly over all unknown model parameters.

nodes.label: Efficiency of an estimator
nodes.description: Compare an unbiased estimator’s variance with the Cramér–Rao lower bound.

nodes.label: Observed Fisher information
nodes.description: Use curvature of the observed log-likelihood to estimate precision.

nodes.label: Bayesian updating
nodes.description: Combines a prior distribution and likelihood to obtain a posterior distribution.

nodes.label: Prior distribution
nodes.description: Represents parameter uncertainty before observing the current data.

nodes.label: Posterior distribution
nodes.description: Represents updated parameter uncertainty after combining prior information and data.

nodes.label: Conjugacy
nodes.description: A prior-likelihood pairing that gives a posterior in the same distribution family.

nodes.label: MAP estimator
nodes.description: The parameter value at the mode of the posterior distribution.

nodes.label: Asymptotic posterior distribution
nodes.description: Connects large-sample Bayesian posteriors with maximum likelihood theory.

nodes.label: Posterior mean and squared-error loss
nodes.description: The posterior mean minimises posterior expected squared error.

nodes.label: Posterior median and absolute-error loss
nodes.description: A posterior median minimises posterior expected absolute error.

nodes.label: Conjugate prior and posterior updates
nodes.description: Reference updates for Beta–Binomial, Gamma–Poisson, Normal and other conjugate pairs.

nodes.label: Confidence intervals
nodes.description: A repeated-sampling procedure designed to cover the true parameter at a stated rate.

nodes.label: Exact confidence intervals
nodes.description: Intervals calibrated from a finite-sample distribution; exact discrete methods may have conservative coverage.

nodes.label: Approximate confidence intervals
nodes.description: Confidence intervals justified by a large-sample approximation.

nodes.label: Confidence level and coverage
nodes.description: Interpret confidence as repeated-sampling coverage of a fixed parameter.

nodes.label: Constructing intervals with pivots
nodes.description: Invert a sampling probability whose reference distribution does not depend on the parameter.

nodes.label: Normal interval: known variance
nodes.description: An exact interval for a Normal mean using the known population standard deviation.

nodes.label: Normal interval: unknown variance
nodes.description: An exact Normal-theory interval using a sample standard deviation and Student-t quantiles.

nodes.label: CLT confidence intervals
nodes.description: Use a large-sample Normal approximation to construct an interval for a population mean.

nodes.label: MLE confidence intervals
nodes.description: Use asymptotic Normality and estimated Fisher information to construct an interval.

nodes.label: Credible intervals
nodes.description: An interval containing a stated amount of posterior probability.

nodes.label: Highest density intervals
nodes.description: A credible interval containing the posterior values with greatest density.

nodes.label: Equal-tailed credible intervals
nodes.description: Use posterior quantiles to leave equal probability in the two excluded tails.

nodes.label: Frequentist hypothesis testing
nodes.description: A decision procedure that evaluates data against a null hypothesis.

nodes.label: Null and alternative hypotheses
nodes.description: Competing parameter statements that define a testing problem.

nodes.label: Test outcomes and errors
nodes.description: Rejection, non-rejection, Type I errors and Type II errors.

nodes.label: p-values
nodes.description: Under the null model, the probability of a result at least as extreme as observed in the direction specified by the alternative.

nodes.label: Power
nodes.description: The probability that a test rejects the null at each possible parameter value.

nodes.label: One-sample z-test
nodes.description: An exact Normal-mean test when the population variance is known.

nodes.label: One-sample t-test
nodes.description: A Normal-mean test using Student’s t distribution when variance is unknown.

nodes.label: Likelihood ratio tests
nodes.description: Tests hypotheses by comparing constrained and unconstrained maximum likelihoods.

nodes.label: Wald tests
nodes.description: Uses an estimator’s approximate Normal distribution and standard error to test a parameter.

nodes.label: Rejection regions and significance levels
nodes.description: Choose rejection outcomes to control the probability of a Type I error.

nodes.label: One-sided and two-sided tests
nodes.description: Choose the direction of the alternative before inspecting the data.

nodes.label: CLT tests for a mean
nodes.description: Use a large-sample reference distribution for a standardised sample mean.

nodes.label: Wilks’ theorem
nodes.description: A chi-squared approximation calibrates the likelihood ratio statistic under regularity conditions.

nodes.label: Bayes factors
nodes.description: Compares how well two hypotheses predict the observed data.

nodes.label: Bayesian hypothesis testing
nodes.description: Compare hypotheses through their posterior probabilities and the predictions of their models.

nodes.label: Prior and posterior hypothesis odds
nodes.description: A Bayes factor multiplies prior odds to produce posterior odds.

nodes.label: Marginal likelihood
nodes.description: Average the likelihood over a proper within-model prior to compare Bayesian models.

nodes.label: Module guide and schedule
nodes.description: The weekly topics, teaching activities and assignment schedule.

nodes.label: Probability distributions
nodes.description: Course PMFs and PDFs, parameter conventions, model choices and an interactive distribution explorer.

nodes.label: Bernoulli
nodes.description: A single binary trial with success probability p.

nodes.label: Binomial
nodes.description: The number of successes in independent trials with a common probability.

nodes.label: Multinomial
nodes.description: Counts in multiple mutually exclusive categories across independent trials.

nodes.label: Poisson
nodes.description: A model for a non-negative count with a rate parameter.

nodes.label: Geometric
nodes.description: Trials until the first success under independent repeated Bernoulli trials.

nodes.label: Negative Binomial
nodes.description: Trials until a specified number of successes, using the course convention.

nodes.label: Uniform
nodes.description: A constant density over a finite interval.

nodes.label: Exponential
nodes.description: A positive waiting-time model parameterised by its rate.

nodes.label: Gamma
nodes.description: A positive distribution with shape and rate parameters.

nodes.label: Inverse Gamma
nodes.description: A distribution on positive values, used as a prior for variances.

nodes.label: Normal
nodes.description: A symmetric bell-shaped distribution parameterised by mean and variance.

nodes.label: Lognormal
nodes.description: A positive variable whose logarithm is Normal.

nodes.label: Chi-squared
nodes.description: The distribution of a sum of squares of independent standard Normal variables.

nodes.label: Student-t
nodes.description: A heavy-tailed reference distribution for Normal mean inference with estimated variance.

nodes.label: F distribution
nodes.description: A reference distribution formed from a ratio of scaled independent chi-squared variables.

nodes.label: Beta
nodes.description: A distribution on the unit interval, useful as a prior for probabilities.

nodes.label: Weibull
nodes.description: A positive lifetime model with a flexible shape.

nodes.label: Multivariate Normal
nodes.description: A joint Normal model described by a mean vector and covariance matrix.

nodes.description: Assessment scope, method selection and links for targeted revision.

nodes.label: Interactive distribution explorer
nodes.description: Explore how distribution parameters change shapes, probabilities and moments.

nodes.label: Practice question bank
nodes.description: Filter practice questions by topic and difficulty, with worked solutions.

nodes.label: Foundational probability practice
nodes.description: Start with events, conditioning, distributions and dependence.

nodes.label: Interpreting statistical methods
nodes.description: Practise choosing methods and interpreting intervals, p-values and power.
